After the corrections all checks pass (measured on 2026-10-07, 21:17): oxfmt correct, build.mjs --strict exit 0 ("16 sections, 70 decisions, 568 findings, 317 terms, 83 demos"), check.mjs 148 passes and "All checks passed", my own Playwright script 62 of 62. Three things stay open for the coordinator before publication or filing: the issue set needs its repairs, the reports of round 7 are not in apps/lab/audit/reports, and 10 raw report files hold the logins of 2 real accounts with their real profile names.

forTheMaintainer: D-PRE-09 is the first answer that the work needs. The filing of the issues waits for it, because its last option files no issue for the 7 findings before the deploy.

This record itself has the steps of the 7 findings: the findings table and the section Access and trust. So each push of the folder apps/lab/audit publishes them. D-PRE-09 decides when, and D-PRE-10 decides if that folder goes to the branch at all.

With an "after the fix" answer to D-PRE-09, the contract pull request with 17 rows opens after the first step of the issue access is deployed. That pull request is the one gate of the plan: 7 issues depend on it.

D-PRE-10, option "Everything": 10 raw report files then show 2 logins and 1 user ID of real accounts of other persons, with invented review data and with names that are equal to the profile names of these accounts (measured). The lab code, the design documents, and the record no longer have these values. If you select "Everything", say in the notes if these 10 files get the new values or stay out.

D-PRE-10 reads your words "put it in a branch" as the complete folder apps/lab: 4,102 files, of which 1,234 are raw reports. You spoke of the lab. The option "Without the report folder" is the narrower reading.

The record reads your last sentence narrowly. Not in it, and so open: the reads of production (D-PRE-04), a report to Ariakit UI (D-PRE-08), security settings (D-PRE-12), and labels (D-PRE-11). Also not in it: one page load of production before and after the placement key (D-LOAD-02). You make it, or you allow it in the notes of D-PRE-04.

The record reads "the implementation" as code changes in pull requests that you review. A merge deploys, and the deploy workflow applies the D1 migrations of that pull request to production. If you want another rule for migrations, say so.

Three things come back to you later with no question today: the number of the capture limit (in a contract pull request), the one command that deletes the comparison Worker in Cloudflare, and the end of an earlier database if read 3 of D-PRE-04 finds one.
9 findings of low severity need a small choice, and no decision asks them: AUTH-08, AUTH-10, AUTH-11, HYG-18, API-15, LIVE-12, INFRA-12, REAL-01, TRUST-06. No step of the plan waits for them.
You can answer in any order. A note alone does not count as an answer, and the label Recommended is not an answer (measured in the page).
